rows.grounds: name of the goddess Ramā (Lakṣmī), invoked as protector
optative/imprecative sense expressing a wish for protection
repeated invocation of protection for the next deity
name of the goddess Māyā, invoked as protector
epithet indicating autonomous rulership of Māyā
emphasizes that Māyā protects through her own agency

items.question: Are Ramā and the self-sovereign Māyā invoked to grant perpetual and autonomous protection?
premises: Ramā is addressed as a goddess who is asked to protect always.
Māyā is addressed as a self-sovereign goddess who is asked to protect.
The term svayam emphasizes Māyā's protection as arising from her own agency.
items.inference: Both Ramā and the self-sovereign Māyā are invoked as divine protectresses, with Ramā granting continual protection and Māyā acting autonomously.
uncertainties: The specific theological sense of svarāṭ as applied to Māyā in this context is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: May the goddess Ramā always protect; may the self-sovereign goddess Māyā herself protect.
